data.description:
## Description

What: Extend the equivalence test to invoke engines in parallel so the full corpus completes under 30s local / 60s CI, and make the budget a tested assertion (the test fails if it exceeds budget). When the full corpus cannot meet the pre-commit budget, provide a fixed-count fast subset selected by measured wall-clock that the pre-commit path runs, while validate.sh --ci runs the full corpus. Why: The performance clause of sc-3 is what makes the gate usable in the pre-commit path consumed by sc-4. Scope IN: parallel invocation across cases/engines, the tested wall-clock budget assertion, the measured-wall-clock fast-subset selection mechanism, and the full-vs-subset split between --ci and pre-commit. Scope OUT: the base correctness assertions (draft-3); the pre-commit hook wiring itself (draft-6/sc-4).

## Done Definitions

- The equivalence test invokes in-scope engines in parallel and a tested assertion fails the run if total wall-clock exceeds 30s local / 60s CI ← Satisfies: sc-3
- A fixed-count fast subset selected by measured wall-clock is defined for the pre-commit path while validate.sh --ci runs the full corpus ← Satisfies: sc-3

## Considerations

- [Performance] Subset selection must be measured (wall-clock), not hand-picked, so the fast set tracks real timing.
- [Reliability] Parallel invocation must keep per-case mktemp isolation to avoid TMPDIR contention masking or causing drift.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a developer, I want the equivalence test to run within a tested wall-clock budget via parallel invocation with a pre-commit fast subset, so that the gate is fast enough to run on every commit without flaking on timeouts.
